item.title: [+1] Understanding the Rural Grocery Store Environment – Challenges and Strategies
item.dc:creator: Charlotte Narjes
item.description:
Narjes's own Extension article: rural Nebraska grocery stores fell from 290 (2016) to 204 (2021), but four towns (Hay Springs, Lynch, Emerson, Utica) have opened cooperative stores since 2021 with two more coming, and a 40-grocer learning cohort launched in 2026. She lays out margin, competition and ownership-transition strategies and names stores as reasons towns stay lively and attract residents. Decline acknowledged, local ownership as the answer, so +1. A counter-example to 'lose the grocery, lose the town'.

“Rural grocery stores are economic drivers, community hubs”
